strategy.summary: Sensorik Ammertal is our sole approved source for the pressure sensor 0-16 bar. It is a sound private mid-size company, acquired by a financial investor in mid-2026, and we are a small customer to it. Head office has frozen all price reductions until December 2027, and the new owner plans to review prices with all customers, so expect it to defend the current price or ask for a 2027 increase backed by the electronic components and labour indices. Our price is only slightly above our bottom-up should-cost, which includes no margin and has a wide error, so margin room looks thin. The open currencies are payment terms, call-off flexibility, binding volume (the forecast is up) and contract length. Our levers against an increase are the contractual notice rule for price changes, its habit of settling well below its ask, should-cost and rising volume. On-time delivery below the contract target is a secondary point; quality is now better than peers. Evidence covers one part only.
strategy.decision_maker: Head office of the new financial investor owner sets price policy (price-reduction freeze). Price changes above a threshold go to the pricing committee, which meets every two weeks. The sales director executes the policy, and the key account manager can settle small moves.

The framework agreement fixes price per calendar year and requires written notice of price changes before year end; it auto-renews unless terminated with notice.

levers.why: It named payment terms and call-off flexibility as open itself; build every sheet around these instead of a price cut.
Price is fixed per calendar year and changes need timely written notice; a late increase request has no contractual basis.
Higher shared forecast volume, offered as binding, is a concrete trade for holding price.
The price already sits above our full-cost estimate and counters the claim that an increase is needed; use it defensively, not to demand cuts.
It habitually settles well below its ask; frame the expectation for any increase request.
The 2026 increase already absorbed part of the cost rise.
Keeping any agreed move under the committee threshold lets the account manager close quickly.
On-time delivery is below the contract target; a fresh fact for a late round. It is above the peer median, so do not lead with it.
Backs the on-time delivery target if delivery is debated.
Anchors any discussion at the current price.

trades.why: Faster payment is the clearest currency with a cash-minded investor owner; trade it for holding price or blocking an increase, in round 1 under the freeze.
Commit binding volume up to the forecast need in exchange for price hold.
Two years of cover during the freeze is worth something to it and protects us against the investor review; 36 months only if free.
Avoid a clause on electronic components at the index peak; accept one only with a base well below the fixed price.
If any increase is unavoidable, push the effective date out, offered as an alternative sheet at a slightly different price.
Keep its standard lead time; do not buy shorter lead time while delivery is already slipping.

price_view.reasoning: A price-reduction freeze, a thin margin over our should-cost, rising driver indices and a single source leave essentially no room for a cut. The realistic goal is to hold the current price or minimise any 2027 increase, using its pattern of settling below ask, the notice rule, volume and payment as currency.

Lead with term packages (payment, volume, length) rather than price demands
Respect its committee cycle and plan rounds accordingly

dont: Do not demand a price reduction head-on under the freeze
Do not threaten termination or a resourcing move we cannot carry out
Do not ask for longer payment plus a price cut

Do not let rounds lapse into silence

strategy.writer_notes: Frame every e-mail as a partnership offer under its new ownership: we accept the freeze on reductions, and in return we seek price stability for the next period. Lead with payment acceleration and punctual payment, binding forecast volume and a two-year term, plus call-off discipline around its shutdown. Point out that prices are fixed per calendar year under the contract and that changes require timely written notice. Use should-cost only defensively against an increase. Keep any concession below its committee threshold where possible so the account manager can close. Expect one real move; after a hold, close or pursue only the term alternatives it names. Clarify tooling ownership internally before any sourcing talk.

findings.text: Price sits only about +2.9% above our should-cost (EUR 23.13 vs 22.47, no margin included). The estimate's error is about 5%, so the margin is thin and could be near zero. There is little room to push price down on cost grounds without hurting a healthy margin.

Cost drivers favour the supplier. Electronic components index PPI-C2611 is +13.5% in 12 months and at its 36-month peak; at weight 0.3 that is about +4.0% on price. Labour cost index LCI-C is +2.7% (weight 0.28), about +0.75%. Together they imply roughly +4.8% for the 0.58 of cost covered, against the +3.1% it already took on 2026-01-01. Caveat: the weights are a category team estimate.

Price history: 22.83 in 2023-24, 22.43 in 2025 (-1.8%), 23.13 in 2026 (+3.1%), so +1.3% since 2023. This is well below the electronics index rise since its 36-month low (+13.7%). Part of the index rise came after the last price was set (PPI was +13.5% from 2025-08), so a further increase request for 2027 is plausible.

The current quote of 2026-09-02 holds the price at 23.13 and says discounts are not possible (head-office directive). The 2026-09-27 call confirmed price reductions are frozen to Dec 2027, but the supplier is open on payment terms and call-off flexibility. Holding the price flat is realistic; a cut is unlikely.
No competing quotes and no RFQ exist, so there is no external price benchmark. The evidence is a single part with a low-precision should-cost.

findings.text: Decision power has moved up and away from the account team. A financial investor bought the company in June 2026 and plans to review prices and terms with all customers. Head office has frozen all price reductions until December 2027. The sales director carries out the freeze; he cannot negotiate it away. Expect price cuts to be refused regardless of the arguments.

There is an approval ladder: any price change above 2 % needs their pricing committee, which meets every two weeks. Moves under 2 % can be settled by the account manager. Larger moves add at least a two-week cycle, so plan rounds and deadlines around it.

The open channels are payment terms and call-off flexibility; the sales director said he was open on both. A new financial owner usually wants cash, so faster payment (contract is 30 days net, our standard 60) and flexible call-offs are the main things we can trade, not price.

The company is financially sound and we matter little to it. Equity ratio is 43.5 %, credit index is stable at 176 and audit grade is VDA 6.3 A. Our spend is about 1.2 % of its turnover of EUR 35 M. It can afford to walk away, so a tone of respect and partnership matters.

Our payment record is a weak spot. We pay 83 % of invoices late, 3.4 days after due on average, with a maximum of 8 days. They may raise this, especially under the new owner. A firm promise of on-time or earlier payment is something we can give them.
They value orderly planning: they asked for January call-offs by 10 December because of the holiday shutdown. Respecting their processes builds goodwill.

The renewal window is open. The contract runs to 2026-12-31 and can be terminated with notice by 2026-10-02. Price changes need 90 days' notice before year end, so a 2027 increase requested after about 2 October is late under the contract. However, we have a single source and they own the tooling, which limits how credible an exit is.

findings.text: Framework agreement ctr:4600070570 covers only part:350050 and runs to 2026-12-31. It extends automatically by 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice. To stop the renewal, notice must be given by 2026-10-02, which is days away as of 2026-09. If we let that date pass, the contract rolls into 2027 on its current terms.

Prices are fixed per calendar year. Any change needs written notice at least 90 days before year end, so by about 2026-10-02 for 2027. If the supplier misses this deadline, it has no contractual basis for a 2027 increase. The new investor owner plans to review prices with all customers (news 2026-06-22), so we should expect such a notice soon.

Payment is 30 days net, against our standard of 60, and the Incoterm is DAP. The supplier already benefits on payment terms. On our side, we pay on average 3.4 days late and 83% of invoices are late; it could raise this.

The quality clause sets a 95% on-time delivery target and a flat EUR 150 per supplier-caused complaint. Its actual on-time delivery is 88%, below target for two years, which gives us a lever. Its ppm has improved (271 against 424 a year earlier).

Renewal history for part:350050:
- 2024: asked +2.1%, settled 0.
- 2025: asked +1.6%, settled -1.8%.
- 2026: asked +4.9%, settled +3.1%.
On average it settles about 2.4 pp below its ask. The concession on the last, larger ask was smaller (1.8 pp). It has told us that changes above 2% need approval from its pricing committee, which meets every two weeks.

The supplier has been our 100% single source since 2015, with no RFQs and no alternative approved source. Tooling ownership is recorded as n/a in sourcing, while the argument library says the supplier owns it. Our spend is about EUR 423k, roughly 1.2% of its turnover. Its finances are sound (equity ratio 43.5%, credit index stable). We are therefore more dependent on it than it is on us.
Its sales director said on 2026-09-27 that price reductions are frozen until December 2027. He was open on payment terms and call-off flexibility, so these are the tradeable currencies.

findings.text: Delivery has slipped and stays below the 95% contract target: rolling OTD fell from 95.7% (2024Q3) to 80% (2026Q1) and has recovered only to 88% (2026Q3). Late lots average 11 days late, with a maximum of 14 days, against a 28-day lead time. That is still above the peers' median of 84.6%, so it is a moderate argument, not a strong one. Requested and confirmed dates are a known data issue.

Quality improved: rolling ppm peaked at 547 (2025Q2) and is now 271 (2026Q3), better than the peers' median of 457. No 8D report is overdue. This argues the supplier's case. Even so, there are 4 supplier-caused QNs in the last 12 months (burr, coating, missing marking), and missing marking and coating defects keep recurring. EUR 150 is recharged per complaint under the quality agreement, a small cost to us.

Volume outlook is up: the 2026-09 forecast is 19,960 pcs for the next 12 months against 18,440 ordered in the last 12 months (+8%). The forecast is shared with the supplier, so we can offer a volume commitment as a trade. Demand has been stable at about 18-20k pcs/yr since 2024.

Price history: EUR 22.83 in 2023-24, EUR 22.43 in 2025 and EUR 23.13 in 2026 (+1.3% overall). The current price is 2.9% above the should-cost of EUR 22.47 (error about 5%). The current orders anchor any increase.

Order handling is clean: 0 stale lines, only 3 rush lines and 3 changed lines, and qty variance of 0.12%. Recent POs were confirmed on the requested dates. Evidence covers a single part only (part:350050).

Faster payment / on-time payment from us (we pay on average 3.4 days late)

arguments.text: Our price barely covers cost: the customer's own bottom-up should-cost of EUR 22.47 sits almost level with our EUR 23.13, and that estimate includes no margin. Any cut would push us to break-even on this part. Their own confidence on the estimate is low (5 %), but it points our way.

Cost drivers are rising. Electronic components PPI is up 13.5 % in 12 months and at its 36-month peak, with about 30 % weight. Labour cost is up 2.7 % and also at its peak, with about 28 % weight. Weighted, that alone justifies roughly +4.8 % on cost. Assembled boards are up 41 %. We are asking to hold the price, not to pass all of this on.
Our price record is moderate. We held flat in 2024 and cut 1.8 % in 2025. Over four years the net change is +1.3 %, well below inflation.
Quality has improved. Rolling ppm fell from 547 to 271, with no overdue 8Ds. We are a solid partner: A-grade VDA 6.3, ISO 9001/14001, 43.5 % equity ratio, and approved source since 2015.
Head office has frozen price reductions until December 2027 under the new ownership. Reductions are outside my authority.

weak_points: On-time delivery is 80-88 % against the contract target of 95 %. Late deliveries average 11 days.
13 supplier-caused complaints, the same defects recurring (marking, coating, burrs).
The 3.1 % increase for 2026 came on top of a should-cost below 2025 levels. Energy prices are down 43 % versus 2022.
The contract requires 90 days' notice before year end for any price change. A 2027 increase notified after early October is weak.
They pay late, but only about 3 days, so that is small leverage for us.
The 'freeze' is a policy, not a cost argument. Pushed hard, it looks like a stance.
We have historically settled well below our ask.
Copper and steel are of minor relevance for a 0.1 kg sensor.
Spend is small for us (about EUR 0.42m of 35m), and the new owner has a margin-review agenda.
wants: Payment on time, or faster: 14 days with a small discount, or strict 30-day punctuality.
Binding annual volume of about 20,000 pcs, matching their forecast.
January call-offs placed before the shutdown (by 10 December), plus a frozen planning horizon.
Possibly an index clause on electronic components instead of a fixed price.
red_lines: No price reduction for 2027, per the head-office directive.
No price below about EUR 22.90 under any package.
No higher chargeback or tighter ppm commitment without price compensation.
Any price move above 2 % needs pricing committee approval, which takes about 2 weeks.
red_team.opening: Thank you for the constructive review. We value the partnership since 2015 and the improved quality this year. Electronic components are up 13.5 % and labour 2.7 %, and our margin on this sensor is thin. Even so, we propose to keep EUR 23.13 unchanged for 2027 rather than pass on costs. To make this sustainable, we would like a 24-month extension with binding volume of about 20,000 pcs and punctual 30-day payment. We are flexible on call-off scheduling, including around our holiday shutdown.

rebuttals.answer: We agree that our own estimate shows little margin room, and we are not asking you to cut below a healthy level. The same estimate also shows the current price already sits above full cost, so it gives no basis for any increase either. Our aim is to keep the current price stable, and we will make that worthwhile for you through payment, volume and term.

The labour and component cost rises are real, and we take them seriously. Part of that rise was already reflected in this year's increase. The headline news on assembled boards and metals describes other products, not your cost structure. Holding the current price is a fair outcome, and we would like to support it with faster payment and a firmer volume commitment rather than an index clause.

We appreciate the moderate record, and it is one reason we value the relationship. Taken over the whole period, though, the price is now above where it started, and the latest renewal was an increase. We therefore see stability from here as balanced rather than as a sacrifice on your side.

We acknowledge the clear improvement in quality and your sound standing, and we want to keep working with you. Complaints still recur on marking, coating and burrs, and these fall under the quality agreement. On-time delivery also remains below the contract target. Our proposal is to lock in what is working on both sides, not to reprice it.

We respect the new owner's policy and are not asking for a reduction. Your sales director told us he is open on payment terms and call-off flexibility, so we would like to build the agreement there. Under the contract, prices stay fixed for the calendar year, and any change needs timely written notice.

press: Could you confirm whether written notice of any price change for next year has been given within the period the framework agreement requires?
We would welcome your plan for bringing on-time delivery back to the contractual target, and we are glad to commit to punctual payment from our side.
Could we agree concrete corrective actions for the recurring marking, coating and burr findings, so the recent improvement holds?
Since our shared forecast is up, would a binding volume over a longer term allow you to keep the current price unchanged?
Would earlier call-offs ahead of your holiday shutdown, together with faster payment, help your planning enough to support price stability?
